## Why This Benchmark Is Included

Canonical reconstruction-based industrial anomaly task.

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Classroom value** | Contrasts reconstruction scoring with supervised classification. |
| **Systems behavior** | Compact dense inference plus feature and score postprocessing. |
| **Benchmark lineage** | Direct MLPerf Tiny workload inheritance. |
| **Model choice** | The autoencoder architecture is fixed upstream. |
| **Dataset choice** | ToyADMOS is fixed upstream. |
| **Quality metric** | ROC AUC and the threshold are fixed upstream. |
| **Published baseline** | MLPerf Tiny reference quality contract |
| **Alternative rejected** | Fashion-MNIST anomaly detection is not the MLPerf workload. |

## Authoritative Sources and Adaptation

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Authority** | MLCommons MLPerf Tiny, ToyADMOS, and DCASE |
| **Model repository** | [open source](https://github.com/mlcommons/tiny) |
| **Model commit** | `4addd0fa08d216e20637637874e084895f289da4` |
| **Dataset record** | [open source](https://zenodo.org/records/3678171) |

**Adaptation boundary:** Fused weights are read from the pinned MLCommons TFLite artifact and loaded into the equivalent PyTorch dense autoencoder. The fixed MLCommons index selects 248 recordings from the immutable ToyADMOS archive, and the pinned upstream librosa recipe generates the exact sliding-window inputs.

## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
uv run mlperf fetch --workload anomaly-detection --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd.json provenance)
uv run mlperf run --workload anomaly-detection --profile max

# quick smoke pass
uv run mlperf run --workload anomaly-detection --profile min

# research envelope
uv run mlperf run --workload anomaly-detection --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

**Reviewer notes:**

- The 0.85 ROC AUC threshold, ToyCar task, 248-recording index, feature recipe, and autoencoder are inherited from MLPerf Tiny.
- The exact PyTorch adapter reproduces the official restricted-set float TFLite AUC at 0.9029100529100529.
- Promotion still requires committed repeated timing evidence on the reference platform.

## Systems Experiment Execution Contract

**Within-run measurement protocol:**

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Primary metric** | inference_seconds |
| **Scenario** | offline |
| **Timing scope** | 10 repetitions of all 48,608 sliding-window autoencoder inferences after model, data, and one complete-set warmup are ready |
| **Included phases** | batched PyTorch autoencoder execution |
| **Excluded phases** | selective source-recording fetch and librosa feature extraction, TFLite weight parsing and PyTorch model construction, binary feature loading and sliding-window view construction, one shape warmup and one untimed complete accuracy-set pass, per-recording reconstruction-score aggregation and ROC AUC computation, report and provenance serialization |
| **Device synchronization** | synchronize immediately before and after the measured inference region |
| **Outer reference runs** | 1 |
| **Outer preconditioning runs** | 0 |
| **Outer inter execution cooldown seconds** | 5 |
| **Repeatability metric** | inference_seconds |
| **Repeatability limit** | 0.05 |

## Results

To make the metric concrete, one run of this benchmark on Apple M5 Max observed `roc_auc` of 0.9029, taking 0.2838 `inference_seconds`.

That is an illustration, not a target and not a score. It comes from a single machine and your hardware will produce different timing. The number that matters is the one your own run reports.

Run the benchmark and read your own report:

```bash
uv run mlperf run --workload anomaly-detection --profile max
```

Every run writes an HTML dashboard for reading, JSON for machine use, CSV for spreadsheets, and a `.provd.json` provenance manifest. Those artifacts carry the quality decision, timing distribution, hardware and software fingerprint, asset digests, and model lineage for the run you performed.

See [Reading Results](../../guide/results.qmd) for how to interpret them.
